items.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate prediction of absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties is important in early-stage drug discovery. Recent work increasingly explores deep neural networks and graph neural networks (GNNs) for molecular property prediction because of their ability to model complex structure-property relationships. However, this increased model complexity often comes at the expense of interpretability, making it difficult to understand the structural basis and confidence of predicted liabilities. We present ToxiLens, an explainable ADMET prediction platform covering 12 endpoints and built to make molecular risk predictions more transparent, actionable, and decision-ready. Each prediction is enriched with structural explanations, uncertainty quantification, applicability-domain assessment, and an endpoint-aware LLM grounded in the model outputs for richer report generation and more informed chatbot interactions. ToxiLens combines SHAP-based substructure attribution, atom-level heatmaps, dynamically calibrated conformal prediction, ensemble uncertainty estimation, similarity-based domain assessment, and a composite Risk Confidence Score that integrates predicted risk, chemical neighborhood support, and bioactivation liability. Models are trained on TDC benchmark datasets using scaffold-based splits with strict separation between training and evaluation. Across 11 production endpoints with CYP2D6 Substrate currently included as a beta endpoint, ToxiLens achieves a mean AUROC of 0.878 and a mean MCC of 0.578, while also providing practical interpretability layers not typically available in black-box ADMET predictors. Most endpoints use 2,077-dimensional descriptor-augmented ECFP4 vectors, while DILI uses a 2,069-dimensional representation. Validation on 100 well-known drugs, including case studies on ketoconazole, fluoxetine, and diclofenac, demonstrates the platform's practical value as an uncertainty-aware screening and interpretation system.</jats:p>
title: ToxiLens: An Explainable ADMET Prediction Platform with Multi-Layered Interpretability and LLM-Powered Clinical Analysis
